To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the neural crest is induced in vitro by a diffusible signal from the neural plate, that the neural crest can be induced by the same signal in the absence of the neural plate, and that this signal is the same as the signal that induces the neural plate.

the neural crest arises as a result of inductive interaction, that the progenitor cells are initially multipotent and progressively restricted, and that neural crest cells are derived from the dorsal neural tube.

neural crest cells can be induced to form by inductive interaction between neural and nonneuronal ectoderm and that the neural crest cells arise from progenitors that are initially multipotent but become progressively restricted to neural crest and then to specific neural crest cell types.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the induction and determination of the neural crest, and the mechanisms underlying the formation of the neural crest and its derivatives.
the mechanisms by which cells are induced to become neural crest cells, and how the progenitor population is restricted to form neural-crest-derived structures.
the cellular and molecular events that occur during the formation of neural crest cells and the development of neural crest derivatives.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the neural crest arises from a population of multipotent progenitor cells that are initially specified by inductive interactions between the neural and the nonneural ectode.

the neural crest arises from the ectoderm by means of an inductive interaction between neural and nonneuronal ectoderm, which is followed by a series of progressive steps that lead to the final differentiation of the neural crest into its various derivatives.

the neural crest is formed by inductive interactions between neural and nonneurall ectoderm, and that these interactions result in the formation of multipotent precursor cells which, in turn, become progressively restricted in phenotype.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the neural crest arises from a multipotent precursor cell population that becomes progressively restricted to form specific derivatives.

inductive interactions are essential for neural crest formation and that neural crest progenitors arise from a multipotent precursor population that becomes progressively restricted to form the neural crest and then to individual neural crest cell types.
inductive interactions between the neural and the nonneural ectoderms are necessary and sufficient to generate neural crest progenitors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
neural crest induction is a multistep process, involving both inductive interactions and cell-autonomous processes.
neural crest cells are not preprogrammed to form a specific phenotype but rather become progressively restricted by inductive interactions.
neural crest cells are not specified in a single step, but rather are generated by means of a series of inductive interactions between the ectoderm and mesoderm.
